text: I don't really care about custom hacky code, I'm sure we all know that, but, I do agree that there needs to be some rules put into place and followed that properly deprecate things, as mentioned in the post above mine, and big changes should always be push"
body:
I don't really care about custom hacky code, I'm sure we all know that, but, I do agree that there needs to be some rules put into place and followed that properly deprecate things, as mentioned in the post above mine, and big changes should always be pushed to a test branch, until it can be compile and typo tested, at the very least. this way, all those "oops, I missed a change here" or, "fixed compile" commits can be rolled into one big commit that still has all the changes, but is one commit, and not 10.

I know I don't submit code as often as others here, but, I think if you go back and look at commits I have made, you will find very few "fix compile" or "fixed a typo" commits associated with them, except for when I didn't have push access and someone else pushed my code, and decided they needed to change something before pushing it... This is due to the fact that I always compile before submitting, I am very careful and almost never make typos, and, I usually do all my work in my own patchqueue or similar environment before submitting.
